caveats: S4 family: original 360/400 acquisition duty; once-only six 8 ms no-edge retry sectors after two 22.5 ms expiries. Any qualified edge cancels rescue. Closed floor holds 360 to 150 ms then fades to minimum by 450 ms, independent of 30-edge threshold. Native missing-feedback count includes all retries, so enabled protection can stop earlier. Bench only.
S4B seeds the ADC handoff guard with the latest real adjacent interval, not the IIR. IIR, first commutation delay and early-pulse rejection are unchanged.
Software-consumed sequential ADC data, not simultaneous scope measurements or rotor direction.
Tail only: 256 samples spaced >=100 us; 96 events include every accepted ADC sample until overwritten. No guarantee of full startup history. Overwritten counts and timestamps are explicit.
When 256 samples are retained, their timestamp span is >=25.5 ms. Short acquisitions or missing fresh samples can leave fewer records; inspect actual span and final sample-to-stop gap.
First no-lock, first post-handoff loss and first full observation are pinned independently; operator-zero and safety stops remain unpinned. Last 16 trial summaries are separate.
PWM/trigger fields read preload registers at consumption, not latched compare values at ADC trigger. Gate/ADC pin analog correctness needs external measurement if software traces remain ambiguous.
Cycle maxima measure inner logger only, not full ISR. No physical protection/flight validation.
Last 16 summaries. S3-D retains separate first no-lock, first post-handoff loss and first complete observation tails. Operator zero and other stops are not pinned.
Observed times are service timestamps, not physical zero-cross timestamps. Current is a filtered software maximum, not peak phase current.

S3 family (including S4): event-led acquisition <= 300 ms; streak counts consecutive ADC-qualified edges, NOT S2 phase-window qualification. Six edges earn <= 1 s observation; first runtime timeout aborts. Not a native stuck-trip proof or flight mode.
